Dosage information

PT-141 dosage

The only established human dose of PT-141 (bremelanotide) is the Vyleesi label dose: 1.75 mg under the skin as needed, for premenopausal women with acquired, generalized HSDD.1 A prescriber sets that dose. No dose is approved for men or postmenopausal women, and research vials have no FDA-reviewed directions.12

This page summarizes published sources for information only. It is not medical advice and does not tell anyone to use a product. Questions about your own health belong with a licensed clinician. For questions about an order or a product, contact us.

Label dosing for Vyleesi

Bremelanotide is approved only as Vyleesi, so its label holds the one set of FDA-reviewed dosing directions.4 The prescriber decides whether it suits a patient and sets the dose within the label.

Label item What the Vyleesi label says
Approved for Premenopausal women with acquired, generalized HSDD1
Dose 1.75 mg in 0.3 mL from a single-dose autoinjector1
Route and site Under the skin of the abdomen or thigh1
Timing As needed, at least 45 minutes before anticipated sexual activity1
Daily limit No more than one dose within 24 hours1
Monthly limit More than 8 doses a month is not recommended1
Stopping rule Stop after 8 weeks if there is no improvement1

Why the label sets these limits

The label says the benefit of a second dose within 24 hours has not been established, and doses close together may add to the rise in blood pressure.1 Few phase 3 patients used more than 8 doses a month.1 More frequent dosing raises the risk of skin darkening and lengthens the time each month when blood pressure is raised.1

Kidney, liver and age

No dose change is advised for mild to moderate kidney impairment (eGFR 30 to 89) or for mild to moderate liver impairment (Child-Pugh A or B).1 The label advises caution in severe kidney or liver impairment and notes that severe liver impairment was not studied.1 In severe impairment, nausea and vomiting may be more frequent or severe.1 Safety and effectiveness have not been established in children or in older adults.1 These statements come from the March 2024 label. On October 23, 2026, FDA approved an update to the label section that holds them, based on a breastfeeding study, and the new text was not posted on Drugs@FDA as of October 25, 2026.144

How women used it in the trials

In the phase 3 trials, women could inject up to 12 times a month, but no more than once per 24 hours.1 The median was 10 injections over the 24-week blinded phase and 12 over the open-label extension.1 Most women used it two to three times a month.1 The approved label later set its advice at no more than 8 doses a month.1

Doses used in published studies

The table lists doses from research studies: who took part, the route and what was tested. These are research conditions, not guidance for any person.

Study Who took part Route Doses tested
Phase 3 trials, 24 weeks (2019) 1,267 premenopausal women with HSDD Under the skin, autoinjector 1.75 mg as needed, no more than once per 24 hours18
Dose-finding trial, 12 weeks (2016) Premenopausal women with sexual dysfunction (327 analyzed) Under the skin 0.75, 1.25 or 1.75 mg, used as desired9
Blood pressure monitoring trial (2017) 397 premenopausal women Under the skin 0.75, 1.25 and 1.75 mg10
Injected-dose studies (2004) Healthy men; men with a poor response to sildenafil Under the skin 0.3 to 10 mg in healthy men; 4 or 6 mg in a crossover design11
Nasal studies (2004) Healthy men; men with mild to moderate erectile dysfunction Nasal Responses above placebo at doses greater than 7 mg3
Combination study (2005) 19 men with erectile dysfunction Nasal, with 25 mg sildenafil 7.5 mg5
Sildenafil non-responder trial (2008) 342 men with erectile dysfunction Nasal 10 mg per attempt, at least 16 attempts at home (paper under a 2023 expression of concern)6
Alcohol interaction study (2017) 24 healthy adults, 12 men and 12 women Nasal Single 20 mg dose7

What the dose studies showed

In the 12-week dose-finding trial, the combined 1.25 and 1.75 mg groups gained 0.7 satisfying sexual events a month, versus 0.2 with placebo (p = 0.018).9 In the 397-woman monitoring trial, the 1.75 mg dose raised systolic blood pressure about 3 mmHg more than placebo in the 4 hours after a dose, and peak rises usually lasted under 15 minutes.10 In healthy men, injected doses produced significant erectile responses at doses above 1 mg.11 With daily dosing, darker skin patches appeared in 38% of participants after 8 days (label) and in more than one third after up to 16 consecutive days (development program review).112 These were safety tests, not treatment schedules.

Reading dose figures

Dose figures across these sources are not directly comparable. The label dose counts bremelanotide itself: 1.75 mg of bremelanotide equals 1.89 mg of bremelanotide acetate.1 Route matters too. A single 20 mg nasal dose reached peak blood levels about 2.5 times those of the 1.75 mg injection.1 After an injection under the skin, bioavailability is about 100%.1

Overdose

No overdoses of Vyleesi have been reported.1 The label says nausea, skin darkening and larger rises in blood pressure are more likely at higher doses.1

No human dose outside the label

The label dose comes from trials of the autoinjector in premenopausal women.1 No dose is approved for men, for postmenopausal women or for enhancing sexual performance.1 Non-prescription 10 mg vials have no approved application and no FDA-reviewed directions.2 A 2026 review of peptides in sexual medicine raises concerns about product quality and dosing variability for melanotan II and related peptides sold through unregulated markets.13 For the risks that rise with frequent use, see PT-141 side effects. For the compound itself, see What is PT-141?, and for the trial outcomes, PT-141 benefits and uses. General principles are in Peptide dosage basics.

Frequently asked questions

Can you take PT-141 every day?

Daily use is not part of the label. The Vyleesi label says not to use more than one dose within 24 hours and does not recommend more than 8 doses a month.1 In a label study where Vyleesi was given daily for 8 days, 38% of participants developed patches of darker skin.1 No FDA-reviewed directions of any kind exist for research PT-141, which has no approved application.2

When is the best time to take PT-141 peptide?

For the approved product, the label says to inject at least 45 minutes before anticipated sexual activity, and never more than once in 24 hours.1 How long each dose keeps working is unknown, so the label lets patients choose their timing based on how they experience the effect and side effects such as nausea.1 No timing is established for non-prescription PT-141.2

How fast does PT-141 take to work?

The Vyleesi label directs injecting at least 45 minutes before anticipated sexual activity.1 After an injection under the skin, blood levels peak at a median of about 1 hour, and the half-life is about 2.7 hours.1 In placebo-controlled studies of men using a nasal form, published in 2004, the first erection came about 30 minutes after dosing.3 None of these figures is an instruction for a person.

How many sprays of PT-141?

No nasal form of bremelanotide is approved, so there is no approved number of sprays.4 Research studies used nasal doses such as 7.5 mg, 10 mg and 20 mg, and a 2004 paper reported erectile responses above placebo at doses greater than 7 mg.5673 These figures describe research conditions, not guidance for people. The approved product is an injection.1
